prompt: I need to add email validation to our user registration. Emails should be validated for proper format, checked for uniqueness against existing users, and rejected if they use a disposable email domain.
assertions: A test file is written BEFORE any implementation code
The test is run and confirmed to FAIL (RED step) before implementation begins
Only minimal code is written to make the failing test pass (GREEN step)
The test is run again and confirmed to PASS after implementation
Refactoring occurs only after tests are green (REFACTOR step)
Additional test cycles cover edge cases (empty email, missing @, disposable domains)

prompt: Fix this bug where duplicate usernames are allowed in user registration. Currently the system accepts duplicate usernames without any error, which causes data integrity issues.
assertions: A test is written that reproduces the bug BEFORE attempting a fix
The reproducing test is run and confirmed to FAIL (proving the bug exists)
The fix is minimal and targeted to make the failing test pass
The test is run again and confirmed to PASS after the fix
Existing tests are run to ensure no regressions
Additional edge case tests are written (case sensitivity, whitespace, empty username)

prompt: Add a discount calculation feature that applies percentage and fixed discounts. A cart should support applying a percentage discount (e.g., 10% off) or a fixed amount discount (e.g., $5 off), and the total should never go below zero.
assertions: Tests are written BEFORE implementation code for each discount type
Each test is run to confirm it FAILS before writing implementation (RED step)
Minimal implementation is written to pass each test (GREEN step)
Multiple red-green-refactor cycles are visible (not a single big-bang implementation)
Refactoring happens only when tests are green
Edge case tests are added: zero discount, discount exceeding total, negative prices, combining discounts
